The two supplied units are BASE-side excerpts of docs/threat-model.yaml (lines 898-1873), covering T-010 through T-046, including T-041 prefix-cache and SEC-035 text. The PR's changed ranges are head-only (lines 43-45, 232-241, 811-841, 2305-2337): header comment, new A-018, new TB-012, and what appears to be T-059. These ranges fall outside the supplied base excerpts, and the patch excerpt is truncated at TB-012. The new head text for TB-012 and T-059 (the add-on hold socket, signature check, leases, machine-lock fallback) was therefore not visible, and I cannot cite any head line or judge it.

Within the supplied base text, there is no observed code change and no weakened control. This is documentation-only and does not alter T-041, T-043 or T-044/T-045 mitigations, so no regression is found in the units I saw.

Open integration questions for the next pass, which needs the head text of the changed ranges:
(1) Does TB-012 correctly state that the same-user owner-only AF_UNIX socket is not a strong authorization boundary? A same-UID attacker could request a hold, so ADV-001 or another local process could cause denial of service to serving (A-018). Is the add-on signature check on the peer enforced (e.g. audit token or code-signing requirement) rather than PID or path-based?
(2) Do hold leases expire, and is there a machine-lock fallback that fails closed or open?
(3) Do the busy fields in heartbeat status interact with routing or attestation, since coordinator handling is declared separate platform work?
(4) Is T-059 consistent with TB-011 and T-057 availability semantics, and does a hold leave attestation or authorization state (A-016) unchanged?

The 'needs_deeper_review' flag is set because of this missing head-side evidence.
